target.title: fix(gateway): deny session-scoped clients the broad sessions.subscribe (per-tab isolation)
target.body:
Hardens the per-tab session isolation added in this branch. Follow-up to my review: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109817#pullrequestreview-4726163583

## What Problem This Solves
A session-scoped (browser-copilot / `SESSION_SCOPED_EVENTS`) connection can call the legacy broad `sessions.subscribe` and join the flat `sessionEventSubscribers` set. `handleTranscriptUpdateBroadcast` (`src/gateway/server-session-events.ts:176-184`) unions that set into `session.message` / `sessions.changed` recipients, and those events aren't in `SESSION_SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS` (`src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts:80`), so they skip the per-tab opt-out filter — delivering **every** session's live transcript to a connection the per-tab model documents as isolated (contra the comment at `server-broadcast.ts:212`).

## Why This Change Was Made
The per-tab boundary is enforced only on the per-session subscription path. A scoped client should never join the broad fanout; it subscribes per session via `sessions.messages.subscribe` (which is all the bundled extension ever calls — `extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/copilot-background.js:374`). Denying the broad path for scoped clients closes the gap at the root without touching delivery mechanics.

Adding the events to `SESSION_SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS` instead over-blocks: those broadcasts don't pass `opts.sessionKeys`, so the per-session filter would also drop *own*-session messages.

## User Impact
Defense-in-depth. Not drive-by-web-page reachable (the extension only uses the per-session path), but a compromised or malicious browser-copilot connection could otherwise read every session's live transcript rather than only its own tab's. No behavior change for the stock extension.

## Evidence
- Dynamic repro on this branch's head (real gateway harness, green on gateway-core / gateway-server / gateway-client) confirmed the cross-session leak pre-fix; post-fix the foreign transcript is no longer delivered.
- Added a regression test in `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts` (browser-copilot broad `sessions.subscribe` rejected + foreign `session.message` not delivered).
- Full `session-message-events` suite stays green (22/22).

target.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory plugins could only contribute synchronous system-prompt text. Memory Wiki therefore persisted its compiled agent digest and claim index in legacy state files, then read those files during prompt assembly. That created a prompt-path filesystem dependency, stale-owner risk, and cache lifecycle behavior outside the plugin state owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one narrow async memory prompt-preparation registration. The agent run validates stable owner and vault-instance identity, loads prepared state before prompt assembly, and hands an immutable snapshot to synchronous prompt builders. Recompilation atomically replaces the snapshot; owner removal deletes its state.

Memory Wiki now stores its rebuildable compiled snapshot as a plugin blob in shared SQLite. Compile publishes one atomic replacement, prompt preparation and queries load the same snapshot, inactive owners are removed at plugin start, and stale legacy files are cleanup-only doctor debt. There is no file migration, polling, watcher, process decoded cache, or prompt-path filesystem I/O.

Context-engine assembly executes inside the same prepared-memory scope, including sandbox context, so custom engines preserve the async supplements without changing the synchronous context-engine contract.

AI-assisted implementation. Maintainer-requested architecture and migration.

## User Impact

Memory Wiki prompts and queries use one lifecycle-owned compiled snapshot. Restarts reload the SQLite blob, recompiles replace it atomically, removed vault owners lose their cached state, and old cache files are safely deleted by doctor instead of being read or migrated.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(openrouter): add model-aware tool schema normalization for proxied providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Models routed through OpenRouter that reject `anyOf`/`oneOf` in tool parameter schemas (Moonshot/Kimi K3, DeepSeek, Google/Gemini) receive raw unsanitized schemas and return HTTP 400 — "provider rejected the request schema or tool payload."

The ClawRouter extension already handles this via `resolveToolFamily()` model-prefix routing, but the OpenRouter extension registers no `normalizeToolSchemas` or `inspectToolSchemas` hooks. Tool schemas pass through verbatim regardless of the downstream provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

Kimi K3 (`moonshotai/kimi-k3`) via OpenRouter fails on tool calls that include `anyOf`/`oneOf` unions in parameter schemas — common in MCP-sourced tools and TypeBox-defined tools. The model handles basic chat completions fine, but 400s on tool payloads.

The root cause: `extensions/openrouter/index.ts` has no tool schema normalization, unlike `extensions/clawrouter/index.ts` which routes models to the correct compat family (`deepseek`, `gemini`, `openai`) based on model ID prefix.

## User Impact

Users running Moonshot/Kimi, DeepSeek, or Google models through OpenRouter will no longer get `400 Provider returned error` on tool calls. The fix applies the same schema normalization that direct provider plugins and ClawRouter already use.

## Evidence

- Observed in production: `moonshotai/kimi-k3` via OpenRouter returns 200 for basic chat but 400 when tools with `anyOf`/`oneOf` schemas are included
- `providerRuntimeFailureKind: "schema"` in gateway diagnostic logs
- ClawRouter already implements the identical pattern at `extensions/clawrouter/index.ts:105-117`
- DeepSeek direct provider uses `buildProviderToolCompatFamilyHooks("deepseek")` at `extensions/deepseek/index.ts:55`
- 7 tests covering Moonshot/Kimi, OpenAI passthrough, Google, and DeepSeek model routing — including 3 regression tests for canonical `openrouter/`-prefixed model IDs
- All OpenRouter extension tests pass

target.title: fix: OpenAI OAuth works behind fake-IP proxies
target.body:
Related: #89491

*AI-assisted (approved by Peter)*

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users behind Clash, Surge, sing-box, or similar fake-IP proxy DNS would have OpenAI OAuth token exchange and refresh rejected when `auth.openai.com` resolved into the RFC 2544 benchmark range or IPv6 unique-local range.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixed OpenAI token endpoint now uses the same narrow fake-IP SSRF policy as OpenAI Realtime: only `198.18.0.0/15` and `fc00::/7` are exempted, and only for the exact `auth.openai.com` hostname. Redirects and all other hostnames remain rejected. No config, environment variable, SDK export, or broad private-network permission is added.

The shared token POST helper applies this policy to both authorization-code and refresh-token exchange. Contributor credit is preserved for @abnershang, whose original #89491 patch identified the proxy-DNS failure mode.

## User Impact

OpenAI OAuth sign-in and token refresh can complete behind supported fake-IP proxies without weakening the guard for other OAuth destinations.

## Evidence

- Resolver-backed regression covers `auth.openai.com` resolving to `198.18.0.42` during authorization-code exchange and `fc00::42` during refresh-token exchange; the same policy rejects `redirect.example.com` before DNS lookup.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts` — 15 tests passed.

target.title: fix(ui): restore first-run setup redirect after reconnect
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where first-time Control UI users could remain on an unconfigured chat screen after `openclaw.setup.detect` failed during a transient Gateway disconnect. The first-run redirect recorded the failed request as its only attempt, so a reconnect could not recover setup guidance.

A real-Gateway reproduction also exposed that Gateway hello canonicalizes the default session alias from `main` to `agent:<id>:main`. The old exact-URL guard treated that internal adoption as user navigation and suppressed the redirect even after a successful incomplete-setup result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detection attempts are scoped to the Gateway client that owns them. Failed attempts become retryable, late results from obsolete clients cannot redirect the page, and a successful current-client result remains terminal across later reconnects.

The default-landing guard now resolves only the `session` query parameter through the existing Gateway session-default contract before comparison. Path, hash, other query parameters, and genuinely different sessions still have to match exactly.

## User Impact

Fresh users who lose the Gateway during the initial setup check are guided to Model Setup after reconnection without reloading the Control UI. Gateway canonicalization of the default chat session no longer blocks that guidance, while explicit session navigation still wins.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** An interrupted first-run setup detection retries against a reconnected real Gateway and redirects after the successful incomplete-setup response.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, Google Chrome, commit `c24e9a79ce17` (tree `e3e0589860b2`, matching the tested checkout).
- **Current-head rebase verification:** GitHub head `3514c93374b1` (tree `92aeb0ca411c`) is based on upstream `bab9a5ede7d`. All four changed-file Git blobs are byte-identical to the real-Gateway proof head; the focused `7/7` unit and `4/4` Chromium E2E checks were rerun on this exact tree.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** A one-shot `node --input-type=module` Playwright harness launched the source Vite Control UI and an isolated real `openclaw gateway run`, killed the Gateway immediately after the first browser `openclaw.setup.detect` frame, restarted the same isolated Gateway, and waited for the visible Model Setup route.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the real `node` + Gateway + Chrome run (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  RESULT gateway_starts=2 browser_sockets=7 detect_requests=3 detect_responses=1 final_path=/settings/model-setup heading=1
  PASS real Gateway reconnect recovered first-run setup redirect
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The browser survived repeated reconnect attempts, retried setup detection until one response completed, changed to `/settings/model-setup`, and rendered the `Connect your AI` heading.
- **What was not tested:** The real Gateway used an isolated local state directory and explicit loopback `auth=none`; a credential-bearing remote Gateway was not used. The separate deterministic Chromium regression continues to use the repository Gateway WebSocket mock.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/model-setup/first-run.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       7 passed (7)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/model-setup.e2e.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)

$ node scripts/ui.js build
✓ built in 6.80s

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json ui/src/app/bootstrap.ts ui/src/pages/model-setup/first-run.ts ui/src/pages/model-setup/first-run.test.ts
EXIT=0

$ git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
EXIT=0
```

The regressions cover failure followed by a replacement client, completion followed by a later replacement, canonical main-session adoption, explicit navigation to another session, one-request deduplication, and one-redirect behavior.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - first-run setup guidance recovers after reconnect.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no persisted state or configuration changes.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - existing admin-scope and advertised-method gates are unchanged.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - Control UI-only lifecycle and navigation comparison.
- Highest-risk area: Treating internal session-key adoption as equivalent without masking real user navigation.
- Mitigation: Only the `session` value is canonicalized with the existing Gateway hello contract; path, hash, other query parameters, and non-default session keys remain strict, with focused tests and real-Gateway proof.

This PR was created with AI assistance. I reviewed the full first-run, Gateway session adoption, route, and cache paths. The repository autoreview helper was attempted with its default Codex engine after the final edits, but the review service failed before producing findings.

target.title: fix(ui): show ClawHub security verdicts on first Skills load
target.body:
Fixes #108647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Control UI > Skills could see a clean, linked ClawHub skill labeled **Unavailable** on first load. The skill still worked, but the misleading security badge made a healthy installation look unverified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Skills page now runs the existing verdict-only loader when it applies a route-provided status report. This hydrates security verdicts without repeating the `skills.status` request and keeps the existing agent-scope and reconnect guards intact. While the verdict request is in flight, a missing verdict is shown as **Refreshing** rather than **Unavailable**; genuine fetch errors and post-fetch missing verdicts still fail closed as **Unavailable**.

## User Impact

Linked ClawHub skills now show their real security status, such as **Clean**, on the first visit to the Skills page. There are no config, Gateway protocol, or migration changes.

## Evidence

- Real Chromium regression: `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/skills/skills-page.browser.test.ts` (1 test passed).
- Skills view coverage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/skills/view.test.ts` (10 tests passed).

Tested from commit `5ae87dad5faa04f8c391fc9768f707cd14941c10` with a freshly built Gateway, isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, loopback-only auth, and a real ClawHub install of `@monikazapisekstudio/socratic-dialog@0.1.3`. Tokens and local paths are redacted below.

target.title: fix(meeting-bot): avoid stale state during transcript and browser recovery
target.body:
Related: #109755

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three deferred meeting-bot reliability issues: transcript cursor polling could replay retained lines under shifted indices after a page gap, untargeted browser recovery could choose a Google sign-in tab before an active meeting tab, and talkback could report ready before microphone state was known.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transcript retention now exposes one contiguous cursor segment and drops a disconnected prefix when page-local history advances. Untargeted recovery prefers adapter-normalized meeting URLs over login fallbacks. Browser-managed local and paired-node talkback now require an explicit unmuted observation; unknown microphone state is transiently blocked as browser-unverified, matching the stricter Teams meetings policy. Delayed paired-node bridge recovery pins the session node and forces the existing-session `chrome.launch: false` path, so `reuseExistingTab: false` cannot open a second call tab. The documented externally managed bridge mode remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Cursor-polling clients no longer receive old transcript lines again after retention gaps. Meeting recovery chooses a real call over a sign-in fallback when both exist. Bots do not claim speech readiness or start realtime audio while microphone state is unknown.

## Evidence

- Added same-epoch and epoch-change transcript gap regressions; 10 focused meeting-bot tests pass.
- Added login-first untargeted recovery regression; 7 Chrome transport tests pass.
- Added unknown-microphone runtime plus paired-node muted, unknown, unmuted, externally managed, and post-unmute recovery regressions; 160 Google Meet tests pass. The recovery regression exercises `reuseExistingTab: false` and proves `/tabs/open` occurs only once.
- Teams sibling proof: 72 tests pass.
- Fresh post-review autoreview on the final recovery delta: no findings, patch correct at 0.93 confidence.
- Full changed-surface Testbox gate passed on pre-rebase head `1cbbb8e590410`: format, API and dependency guards, four typecheck lanes, core and extension lint, runtime guards. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxrqrkxx86be279fs0fxjkfb`; run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29606528421. Rebasing to `bb4d2054a16bd` changed ancestry only; all nine reviewed files are byte-identical.

## Maintainer Decision

Unknown microphone state is intentionally fail-closed for browser-managed talkback. It remains a transient `browser-unverified` state until Meet explicitly reports `micMuted: false`; muted, unknown, and manual-action states cannot start realtime audio.

Live signed-in Meet/audio validation was not available: the connected nodes do not expose the `google-meet` capability, and the sole approved Meet-capable node is offline. The browser-facing contracts are covered by focused integration tests.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running gateway processes could keep growing the model-pricing cache when refreshes see many dynamic provider/plugin model rows, eventually increasing heap pressure and risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache is capped at the shared gateway pricing state boundary so every refresh replacement path is bounded consistently. target.title: fix(googlechat): surface reply send failures instead of silently dropping chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`deliverGoogleChatReply` (extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts:79-109 on `main`) wrapped every chunk send in a try/catch that only logged the error and kept looping. Two silent-loss paths resulted:

1. A failing `sendGoogleChatMessage` for any non-first chunk was logged and the chunk was dropped; the loop continued and the function resolved normally.
2. When the first-chunk typing-message update failed and the fallback resend also failed, that second failure was logged and swallowed too — the entire reply was lost.

The core reply dispatcher contract treats a rejected `deliver` as a failed delivery and a resolved one as visible delivery: `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483` awaits `options.deliver(...)` and only routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` in `.catch`. Resolving after a swallowed send error therefore reported the turn as delivered while the user saw nothing (or only part of the reply).

## Why This Change Was Made

Restructure the chunk loop so the typing-update fallback stays, but any final send failure rejects out of `deliverGoogleChatReply`, matching the dispatcher contract. The typing-update catch is kept because a stale typing placeholder is recoverable — the same chunk is immediately resent as a new message, and only that resend failing is a real delivery failure. This mirrors the LINE sibling, which documents that a lost bubble "must surface as a partial delivery, not silent success" (extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts:217-219), and the same-channel precedent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96646 ("throw on non-ok instead of parsing error body as success").

Fix classification: channel delivery error-propagation fix, additive behavior change only on the failure path; no config, SDK, or core changes.

## User Impact

- Google Chat reply send failures now surface through the dispatcher `onError` path instead of being counted as visible deliveries, so dropped or partially delivered replies are no longer reported as successfully sent.
- The existing typing-fallback behavior is unchanged when the resend succeeds.

## Evidence

### Integration-backed failure-path proof (real HTTP stack, loopback stub)

New committed regression test `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts` drives the production stack end to end against a local HTTP impersonator of the Google Chat API: `deliverGoogleChatReply` → `sendGoogleChatMessage` → `withGoogleChatResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → real `google-auth-library` JWT signing and token exchange. Only global `fetch` is stubbed (rerouting `chat.googleapis.com` / `oauth2.googleapis.com` to `127.0.0.1`); the service-account key is a throwaway RSA key generated in-process, the stub issues the token, and the stub answers the second `spaces.messages` create with a real HTTP 500 error envelope. The deliver/onError wiring mirrors `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts:408-429`, and the outcome labels follow the dispatcher contract in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483`. No real credentials, endpoints, or user data anywhere.

Standalone transcript of the same flow (three-chunk reply, second create → 500), after the fix:

```
stub: POST /token (grant=jwt-bearer) -> 200 access_token=ya29.stub-token (redacted)
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #2 text="Second chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: [default] Google Chat text reply failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,"message":"stub: backend unavailable","status":"INTERNAL"}}
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=failed-deliver
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=2 createStatuses=[200,500] patchAttempts=0 onErrorCalls=1
```

Same stub, same input, pre-fix `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` from `origin/main` (reverse control): the 500 is logged and swallowed, the third chunk is still sent, and the dispatcher records the reply as delivered with `onError` never firing:

```
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #2 text="Second chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: Google Chat message send failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,...}}
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #3 text="Third chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=delivered
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=3 createStatuses=[200,500,200] patchAttempts=0 onErrorCalls=0
```

Second after-fix scenario (typing placeholder already deleted upstream: `PATCH .../messages/typing` → 404, resend create → 500): the recoverable placeholder failure is logged, the resend failure rejects and reaches `onError`:

```
stub: PATCH /v1/spaces/AAA/messages/typing -> 404 (typing placeholder gone)
runtime.error: Google Chat message send failed: Error: Google Chat API 404: {"error":{"code":404,...}}
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: [default] Google Chat text reply failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,...}}
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=failed-deliver
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=1 createStatuses=[500] patchAttempts=1 onErrorCalls=1
```

| | BEFORE (`origin/main` source) | AFTER (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Stub observed | 3 real `POST .../messages` (`[200,500,200]`) | 2 real `POST .../messages` (`[200,500]`), third chunk never attempted |
| `deliver` result | resolved — reply counted delivered, chunk 2 silently dropped | rejected with `Google Chat API 500: {...}` |
| Dispatcher outcome | `delivered`, `onError` never fires | `failed-deliver`, `onError` fires once with the API error |
| New integration test | 2 of 3 tests fail (reverse-verified) | 3/3 pass |

### Before vs after (same regression tests, same mocks)

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Non-first chunk send rejects | resolves; chunk dropped, loop continues | rejects with the send error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend rejects | resolves; whole reply lost | rejects with the resend error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend succeeds | resends, resolves (kept) | resends, resolves (unchanged) |

### Contract chain (source verified on `main`)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Channel deliver | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 408-421 | `deliver: async (payload) => { await deliverGoogleChatReply(...) }` |
| Channel onError | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 425-429 | `[accountId] Google Chat <kind> reply failed: <err>` |
| Swallowed failure (pre-fix) | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | 95-107 | catch logs, drops chunk / swallows fallback failure, loop resolves |
| Dispatcher contract | `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts` | 476-483 | `await options.deliver(...)`; only `.catch` routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` |
| Sibling precedent | `extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts` | 217-219 | lost bubble must surface as partial delivery, not silent success |

### Control-red (reverse verification)

Reverting only `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` to `origin/main` while keeping the new tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts
 Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
   × surfaces a failed non-first chunk send as a dispatcher-visible delivery failure
   × rejects when the resend after a typing-placeholder update failure also fails
     → Expected: "failed-deliver" / Received: "delivered" (500 logged and swallowed)
```

The mock-level suite shows the same inversion (`2 failed | 4 passed` on pre-fix source). With the fix restored, both suites are green.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Full extension suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat` → 211 passed / 1 failed (212 total); the single failure (`setup.test.ts:236`, service-account setup-wizard flow) also fails on a clean `origin/main` checkout without this change (pre-existing, unrelated — same failure observed in the previous proof round before this PR touched anything).

### What was not tested

- A real Google Chat workspace send (requires live service-account credentials); the loopback impersonator covers the full production HTTP/auth/guard stack instead, including the real error-envelope parsing that builds the `Google Chat API 500: ...` message.
- Full-repo `tsgo` lanes left to CI.

### Impact-surface review

| File | Change | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | chunk loop restructured; send failures now propagate | covered by mock-level + integration regression tests |
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts` | +2 rejection tests; existing fallback test unchanged and green | 6/6 pass |
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts` | new integration suite: real HTTP stub, before/after dispatcher-visible outcomes | 3/3 pass; 2 fail on pre-fix source |

### Lint / typecheck / format

```
$ oxlint extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts   # exit 0
$ tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json (fresh buildinfo)                                                                                                    # 0 errors
$ oxfmt --check <all touched files>                                                                                                                                         # correct format
$ git diff --check origin/main                                                                                                                                              # clean
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Linux Node 24 CI flake where the exec output-capture test could report `termination: "timeout"` instead of `"exit"` when the shared Vitest worker was heavily loaded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failing case tests bounded tail capture, not timeout behavior. It now leaves command lifetime to Vitest's test deadline instead of racing an unrelated 2-second command watchdog against the delayed child `exit` event. The dedicated global-timeout and no-output-timeout assertions remain unchanged.

No runtime change is needed: the failed run captured the expected stdout and stderr before the overdue global watchdog won the event-loop ordering race, and Execa 9.6.1 waits for the observed child `exit` event after cancellation.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Maintainers get deterministic CI coverage for bounded exec output capture under loaded Linux runners.

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

target.title: fix(telegram): reject malformed table spans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram rich-block table rendering could treat malformed HTML table span attributes as valid numbers when assistant-authored HTML contained values like `colspan="2x"` or `rowspan="3y"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram table span parsing now accepts only complete decimal integer span values and keeps malformed spans as ordinary one-cell table entries. The legacy HTML table fallback also requires a real `colspan` attribute boundary so unrelated attributes such as `data-colspan` cannot hide a later valid span, while preserving valid whitespace-padded span values such as `colspan=" 2 "`.

Related independent bug-family PRs: this is part of a strict external numeric-token parsing wave; each PR is independent, based on `upstream/main`, and has no merge dependency on the others.

## User Impact

Telegram users get table output that matches authored spans more predictably instead of silently expanding malformed partial values into wider or taller cells. Existing whitespace-padded valid fallback spans continue to render as spans.

target.title: fix(slack): stabilize tool-result reaction tests
target.body:
Related: #109910

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where five Slack reaction assertions in the tool-result suite intermittently observed zero reaction calls during the full Slack test lane, despite the underlying turn reaching the reply resolver. The failures reproduced on clean `main` in 2 of 3 full-suite runs.

target.title: fix(auth): decouple plugin synthetic-auth from profile fallback for gateway attempts (#110103)
target.body:
Closes #110103

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where anthropic-vertex users whose only credential is Google ADC (Application Default Credentials) hit "No API key found" on gateway-routed model calls, even though the same synthetic ADC auth resolves under `--local` and the plugin itself confirms it works.

## Why This Change Was Made

A gateway direct-attempt sets `allowAuthProfileFallback: false` so an unrelated stored-profile store cannot replace or pre-reject the immutable env/config source. `resolveApiKeyForProvider` was gating the provider plugin synthetic-auth hook on that same flag (`allowPluginSyntheticAuth: params.allowAuthProfileFallback !== false`), so turning off profile fallback also silenced the plugin hook and the gateway path failed for ADC-only providers.

This adds a distinct `allowPluginSyntheticAuth` flag on `resolveApiKeyForProvider` and `getApiKeyForModel`. It defaults to the previous coupled value so existing callers are unchanged, and the two gateway direct-attempt seams (`runtime-plan/resolve-auth` and the embedded-agent-runner `auth-controller`) pass it `true`. Stored-profile discovery stays gated by `allowAuthProfileFallback`, so the prepared-attempt isolation invariant is preserved: enabling plugin synthetic-auth does not re-open the profile store.

## User Impact

anthropic-vertex and other GCP-ADC-only providers now authenticate over the gateway route the same way they already do under `--local`. No behavior change for any provider that resolves through a stored profile or an env/config key.

## Evidence

Two regression tests added in `src/agents/model-auth.test.ts`:
- a gateway-isolated attempt (`allowAuthProfileFallback: false`) now resolves plugin synthetic auth
- stored-profile isolation still holds: a stored api-key profile stays unresolved when profile fallback is off, even with `allowPluginSyntheticAuth: true`

Local run of the full model-auth suite (vitest 4.1.10, Node 24 on Windows):

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  162 passed (162)
```

## AI disclosure

This change was written with Claude (Opus 4.8). I reviewed the diff, ran the tests locally, and take responsibility for the contents.

target.title: refactor(channels): move inbound turn execution into core
target.body:
Related: #109316

Follow-up to #109716.

## What Problem This Solves

Bundled message channels still owned the core execution half of inbound turns: session recording, dispatcher construction, durable-delivery handling, retry plumbing, reply pipelines, and final lifecycle callbacks. That kept deprecated low-level compatibility calls alive as internal architecture even after the marker sweep reached zero removable declarations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now owns the complete inbound turn lifecycle. Channel adapters return data-only turn plans containing normalized context plus transport delivery facts; the core runner performs recording, dispatch, retry, durable delivery, typing/reaction lifecycle composition, and finalization. Feishu, iMessage, Matrix, Mattermost, Microsoft Teams, QQBot, Signal, Telegram, and WhatsApp now use that path. Special native Mattermost interactions use the focused core reply seam instead of rebuilding lifecycle logic.

The modern buffered/plain dispatch contracts and channel turn plan now accept an optional resolver-only `configOverride`. This preserves Microsoft Teams sender-timezone overrides without replacing the base dispatch policy config; it is an additive non-deprecated SDK field.

Shipped Plugin SDK declarations remain byte-compatible. A ratcheted guard rejects bundled production use of prepared-turn callbacks, pre-dispatch failure callbacks, and low-level dispatcher lifecycle calls.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. External plugins keep the shipped compatibility window. Maintainers get transport-thinner channels, one core execution path, and a hard zero budget for internal deprecated channel lifecycle calls.

Non-test TypeScript using the task's `*.test.ts` exclusion: **+1984 / -2004, net -20 lines**.

| DEAD | 0 remaining | Caller and SDK-surface searches found no removable remaining declaration. No removed-symbol tests were rewritten. |

Raw marker lines and declarations are different units: a declaration may carry several deprecated members or be re-exported through public barrels.

target.title: fix(sessions): Windows SQLite archive fsync no longer loops on EPERM
target.body:
Closes #110152

AI-assisted: implemented with Cursor/Grok under human direction and review. Workflow: issue-driven fix; reproduced the Windows fsync EPERM on this machine, then kept one writable exclusive-create descriptor through write+fsync.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users running SQLite-backed sessions would see repeated "SQLite session maintenance cleanup failed" warnings with EPERM from fsync, while the gateway stalled for tens of seconds and never finished cleaning the same stale session IDs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive materialization used to write the temp file, reopen it read-only, then fsync. On Windows that read-only fsync fails with EPERM, so the archive path aborts before the row-delete transaction and the same stale rows keep getting re-planned. The fix keeps the original exclusive writable descriptor through write and fsync, then renames into place. Directory fsync stays best-effort. Off-main-thread compression/IO for large archives is left as a follow-up.

## User Impact

Windows gateways can finish SQLite transcript archival and stop looping on the same cleanup set. Non-Windows behavior stays on the same durable archive-before-delete path.

## Evidence

Live Windows runtime repro (Node v24.15.0, Windows 11) of the descriptor-mode failure described in #110152:

```text
{"mode":"r","ok":false,"code":"EPERM","errno":-4048,"syscall":"fsync","node":"v24.15.0"}
{"mode":"r+","ok":true,"node":"v24.15.0"}
{"pattern":"writable-fd","ok":true,"node":"v24.15.0"}
```

Focused tests on this worktree after the fix:

```text
pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.session-lifecycle-mutation.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Includes a Windows-only regression that asserts fsync on an "r" handle throws EPERM -4048, plus a materializeSqliteSessionStateDeletePlans archive write that exercises the real writable-descriptor path.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in crabline injection
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109992

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the `postCrablineInbound()` error path. When a Crabline inbound injection returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body ReadableStream is now explicitly cancelled before throwing the error, preventing an unread stream resource leak.

**What NOT changed**: No change to the happy path — successful responses still pass through to the complete handler as before. No change to the Crabline injection logic, request construction, or error message format. No new dependencies added.

**Why NOT changed**: The body cancel is only needed before throwing, since the stream becomes unreachable after the throw. On success the body is not consumed by this function — the entire response is forwarded — so no cancel is required on the ok path.

**merge-risk**: Minimal — the pattern `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` is a standard no-op on success and a no-throw guard on failure. It affects only the single error path in `crabline-transport.ts`. Zero risk of regression on the ok path.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a Crabline inbound injection HTTP request returns a non-ok response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is left unread, causing a potential resource leak (unconsumed ReadableStream). Node.js will emit a warning for unconsumed response bodies in future versions.

**Root Cause**: `postCrablineInbound()` throws immediately in the `if (!response.ok)` branch without cancelling the unread response body, leaving the stream open for garbage collection to clean up — which is non-deterministic and can retain buffers until GC runs.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the error path to eagerly release the stream. The `cancel()` method (Fetch API standard) releases the stream's resources. The `?.` optional chaining guards against a null body (e.g., 204 No Content responses or server errors that omit a body). The `.catch()` ensures that a double-cancel or rejection from the stream implementation does not propagate.

## Evidence

### Mocked body cancel behavior (covers the code contract)

The following edge cases were verified with a TypeScript demo exercising the exact same `body.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` pattern:

```
--- Body cancel before throw ---
Body cancelled before throw: YES ✅
Error: Crabline injection failed (502)

--- Cancel rejection handled ---
Cancel rejection suppressed: ✅
Error: Crabline injection failed (400)

--- Null body safe ---
Null body cancel: safe ✅

--- Double cancel safe ---
Double cancel: safe ✅ (n=2)

COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0
```

### Crabline transport unit tests (17/17 pass)

All existing crabline transport tests pass with the fix applied, confirming no regression on the success path:

```

 ✓ crabline transport > configures distinct Telegram actors for canonical sender allowlist flows 66ms
 ✓ crabline transport > rejects canonical sender-policy flows on non-Telegram Crabline bridges 2ms
 ✓ crabline transport > injects Telegram native commands through the shared transport adapter 37ms
 ✓ crabline transport > observes Telegram preview edits through the shared transport adapter 41ms
 ✓ crabline transport > configures OpenClaw's Slack plugin against a Crabline local provider server 15ms
 ✓ crabline transport > injects inbound messages through Crabline and mirrors Slack sends ... 36ms
 ✓ crabline transport > configures OpenClaw's WhatsApp plugin against a Crabline Baileys ... 4ms
 ✓ crabline transport > injects WhatsApp inbound messages through Crabline into normalized state 26ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Signal config and normalizes transport targets 29ms
 ✓ crabline transport > normalizes native Signal JSON-RPC sends into outbound state 27ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Mattermost config and normalizes transport targets 41ms
 ✓ crabline transport > normalizes native Mattermost post creation into outbound state 39ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 69ms
 ✓ crabline transport > normalizes native Matrix room message sends into outbound state 47ms
 ✓ crabline transport > configures Zalo and normalizes native message sends 42ms
 ✓ crabline transport > injects inbound messages through Crabline and mirrors Telegram ... 62ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

### Real QA Lab runtime evidence

The actual failure scenario (a Crabline inbound injection returning HTTP 502/400 in a QA Lab run) requires:
- A running QA Lab instance with a Crabline adapter configured against a live provider
- A provider or network condition that causes the admin inbound injection to return a non-2xx status

This is not reproducible in a local dev environment without the full QA Lab runtime infrastructure. The mock-based demo above verifies the exact code contract (`response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` semantics), and the existing unit tests confirm no regression on the success path.

## Tests and validation

- `scripts/evidence-crabline.ts` — TypeScript demo exercising the `body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` pattern with mocked body objects, covering cancel-before-throw, cancel rejection, null body, and double cancel.
- `docs/.local/pr-109992/verify.log` — terminal session capture via `script -q` containing `COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0`.

target.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite
target.body:
Related: #98236

AI-assisted: yes. The complete branch diff was reviewed with the repo autoreview workflow; all accepted/actionable findings were addressed before landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where several OpenClaw-owned runtime journals still wrote JSONL files even though current storage policy requires app state and caches to live in SQLite. Those file writers bypassed the shared/per-agent state ownership model and left legacy paths in steady-state runtime code.

The session/transcript store was deliberately excluded because #98236 owns that SQLite flip.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remaining state writers now use the narrowest existing SQLite owner: shared diagnostic events for core audit journals, Memory Core plugin state for memory-host events, and the per-agent database for ACP parent-stream diagnostics. Legacy persistent audit/event files import only through explicit `openclaw doctor --fix` migrations. Core and plugin doctor imports require exclusive state ownership for their full read/import/archive window, preflight SQLite capacity, verify imported rows, sanitize retired sources, and only then archive them. ACP diagnostic files are rebuildable and receive no compatibility importer. There are no runtime fallback readers or dual writes.

### Audit classification

| Surface | Observed role | Policy classification | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config/io.audit.ts` (`logs/config-audit.jsonl`) | Core config-write/observe audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `config-audit` | Migrated; redacted records; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/system-agent/audit.ts` (`audit/system-agent.jsonl`, retired Crestodian path) | Core system-agent mutation audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `system-agent-audit` | Migrated; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/memory-host-sdk/events.ts` (`memory/.dreams/events.jsonl`) | Memory recall/promotion/dream event state consumed by status, public artifacts, and Memory Wiki | Memory Core plugin KV in shared SQLite | Migrated with atomic cursor + event + retention writes, namespace-global ordering, 8 KiB payload and 10,000-row bounds, and isolated cursor state capped at 1,000 rows; doctor validates the full source, preflights capacity, and defers all import on malformed or unsafe input |
| `memory/events/memory-host-events.jsonl` | Public memory-event artifact consumed by Memory Wiki and bridge clients | Named, derived export artifact; SQLite remains authoritative | Preserved as a real filesystem path for existing consumers; latest 1,000 events, capped at 1 MiB; atomically refreshed only when content changes |
| `src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` (`*.acp-stream.jsonl`) | Child-session ACP parent-stream diagnostic state | Per-agent DB, `acp_parent_stream_events` | Migrated; rows are session-owned and cascade on session deletion; writes batch synchronously, retry with backoff, and cap pending diagnostics; old transient files are not imported |
| `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` | Reads legacy/archive transcript JSONL; rollups already use per-agent SQLite | Excluded session/transcript area; no JSONL writer | Left unchanged; #98236 owns session/transcript storage |
| `src/security/fix.ts` | Repairs permissions on excluded transcript artifacts | Excluded session/transcript maintenance; no writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts` | Names/filter rules inside backup production | Named backup artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/agents/cache-trace.ts`, `src/agents/anthropic-payload-log.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.raw-stream.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-*`, channel delivery trace | Explicit opt-in traces, raw provider capture, or support bundles | Named diagnostic/log artifacts | Left unchanged |
| CLI runner/Claude session files, transcript/session-manager paths, hooks, compaction checkpoints, session inspection/branching | Provider/external-tool contracts or the excluded session/transcript surface | External tool contract or #98236-owned session artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/trajectory/{runtime-file,paths,cleanup,types}.ts` | SQLite runtime plus explicit trajectory export/legacy discovery | Named export artifact; no steady-state JSONL app-state writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/{exec-host,exec-approvals}.ts` and node CLI JSONL references | Framed IPC/socket payloads | External wire contract, not file state | Left unchanged |
| `src/plugin-sdk/api-baseline.ts` | Generated SDK inspection output | Generated developer artifact | Left unchanged; tracked checksum regenerated for this SDK surface |
| Schema/help/status/tool-display/workshop references and test-support/harness files from discovery | Format names, readers, fixtures, or temporary external/session scratch | No remaining production file writer | Left unchanged |

The post-change discovery still finds legacy migration constants and legitimate artifact/wire/session references, but no additional non-session OpenClaw-owned runtime JSONL writer.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two fixes:

1. **QA Lab HTTP client:** Two HTTP helper functions (`getJson`, `getJsonNoStore`) throw on non-ok responses without canceling the response body stream, potentially leaking connections.

2. **Google Vertex ADC:** `JSON.parse` on credential file content could throw an unhandled `SyntaxError` if the file contains malformed JSON.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. The QA Lab HTTP functions now cancel the response body before throwing, matching the established codebase pattern.
2. The Vertex ADC credential parser wraps `JSON.parse` in try-catch to produce a descriptive error message instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

## User Impact

- QA Lab: No user-visible behavior change.
- Vertex ADC: Operators get a clear error message when ADC credential files have invalid JSON.

## Evidence

- Both fixes follow established patterns in the codebase.
- The `response.body?.cancel()` pattern matches `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and others.

---

target.title: fix(googlechat): surface reply send failures instead of silently dropping chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`deliverGoogleChatReply` (extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts:79-109 on `main`) wrapped every chunk send in a try/catch that only logged the error and kept looping. Two silent-loss paths resulted:

1. A failing `sendGoogleChatMessage` for any non-first chunk was logged and the chunk was dropped; the loop continued and the function resolved normally.
2. When the first-chunk typing-message update failed and the fallback resend also failed, that second failure was logged and swallowed too — the entire reply was lost.

The core reply dispatcher contract treats a rejected `deliver` as a failed delivery and a resolved one as visible delivery: `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483` awaits `options.deliver(...)` and only routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` in `.catch`. Resolving after a swallowed send error therefore reported the turn as delivered while the user saw nothing (or only part of the reply).

## Why This Change Was Made

Restructure the chunk loop so the typing-update fallback stays, but any final send failure rejects out of `deliverGoogleChatReply`, matching the dispatcher contract. The typing-update catch is kept because a stale typing placeholder is recoverable — the same chunk is immediately resent as a new message, and only that resend failing is a real delivery failure. This mirrors the LINE sibling, which documents that a lost bubble "must surface as a partial delivery, not silent success" (extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts:217-219), and the same-channel precedent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96646 ("throw on non-ok instead of parsing error body as success").

Fix classification: channel delivery error-propagation fix, additive behavior change only on the failure path; no config, SDK, or core changes.

## User Impact

- Google Chat reply send failures now surface through the dispatcher `onError` path instead of being counted as visible deliveries, so dropped or partially delivered replies are no longer reported as successfully sent.
- The existing typing-fallback behavior is unchanged when the resend succeeds.

## Evidence

### Integration-backed failure-path proof (real HTTP stack, loopback stub)

New committed regression test `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts` drives the production stack end to end against a local HTTP impersonator of the Google Chat API: `deliverGoogleChatReply` → `sendGoogleChatMessage` → `withGoogleChatResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → real `google-auth-library` JWT signing and token exchange. Only global `fetch` is stubbed (rerouting `chat.googleapis.com` / `oauth2.googleapis.com` to `127.0.0.1`); the service-account key is a throwaway RSA key generated in-process, the stub issues the token, and the stub answers the second `spaces.messages` create with a real HTTP 500 error envelope. The deliver/onError wiring mirrors `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts:408-429`, and the outcome labels follow the dispatcher contract in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483`. No real credentials, endpoints, or user data anywhere.

Standalone transcript of the same flow (three-chunk reply, second create → 500), after the fix:

```
stub: POST /token (grant=jwt-bearer) -> 200 access_token=ya29.stub-token (redacted)
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #2 text="Second chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: [default] Google Chat text reply failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,"message":"stub: backend unavailable","status":"INTERNAL"}}
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=failed-deliver
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=2 createStatuses=[200,500] patchAttempts=0 onErrorCalls=1
```

Same stub, same input, pre-fix `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` from `origin/main` (reverse control): the 500 is logged and swallowed, the third chunk is still sent, and the dispatcher records the reply as delivered with `onError` never firing:

```
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #2 text="Second chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: Google Chat message send failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,...}}
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #3 text="Third chunk of the assistant reply." -> 200
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=delivered
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=3 createStatuses=[200,500,200] patchAttempts=0 onErrorCalls=0
```

Second after-fix scenario (typing placeholder already deleted upstream: `PATCH .../messages/typing` → 404, resend create → 500): the recoverable placeholder failure is logged, the resend failure rejects and reaches `onError`:

```
stub: PATCH /v1/spaces/AAA/messages/typing -> 404 (typing placeholder gone)
runtime.error: Google Chat message send failed: Error: Google Chat API 404: {"error":{"code":404,...}}
stub: POST /v1/spaces/AAA/messages #1 text="First chunk of the assistant reply." -> 500
runtime.error: [default] Google Chat text reply failed: Error: Google Chat API 500: {"error":{"code":500,...}}
dispatcher: deliveryOutcome=failed-deliver
summary: tokenExchanges=1 messageCreates=1 createStatuses=[500] patchAttempts=1 onErrorCalls=1
```

| | BEFORE (`origin/main` source) | AFTER (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Stub observed | 3 real `POST .../messages` (`[200,500,200]`) | 2 real `POST .../messages` (`[200,500]`), third chunk never attempted |
| `deliver` result | resolved — reply counted delivered, chunk 2 silently dropped | rejected with `Google Chat API 500: {...}` |
| Dispatcher outcome | `delivered`, `onError` never fires | `failed-deliver`, `onError` fires once with the API error |
| New integration test | 2 of 3 tests fail (reverse-verified) | 3/3 pass |

### Before vs after (same regression tests, same mocks)

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Non-first chunk send rejects | resolves; chunk dropped, loop continues | rejects with the send error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend rejects | resolves; whole reply lost | rejects with the resend error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend succeeds | resends, resolves (kept) | resends, resolves (unchanged) |

### Contract chain (source verified on `main`)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Channel deliver | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 408-421 | `deliver: async (payload) => { await deliverGoogleChatReply(...) }` |
| Channel onError | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 425-429 | `[accountId] Google Chat <kind> reply failed: <err>` |
| Swallowed failure (pre-fix) | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | 95-107 | catch logs, drops chunk / swallows fallback failure, loop resolves |
| Dispatcher contract | `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts` | 476-483 | `await options.deliver(...)`; only `.catch` routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` |
| Sibling precedent | `extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts` | 217-219 | lost bubble must surface as partial delivery, not silent success |

### Control-red (reverse verification)

Reverting only `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` to `origin/main` while keeping the new tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts
 Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
   × surfaces a failed non-first chunk send as a dispatcher-visible delivery failure
   × rejects when the resend after a typing-placeholder update failure also fails
     → Expected: "failed-deliver" / Received: "delivered" (500 logged and swallowed)
```

The mock-level suite shows the same inversion (`2 failed | 4 passed` on pre-fix source). With the fix restored, both suites are green.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Full extension suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat` → 211 passed / 1 failed (212 total); the single failure (`setup.test.ts:236`, service-account setup-wizard flow) also fails on a clean `origin/main` checkout without this change (pre-existing, unrelated — same failure observed in the previous proof round before this PR touched anything).

### What was not tested

- A real Google Chat workspace send (requires live service-account credentials); the loopback impersonator covers the full production HTTP/auth/guard stack instead, including the real error-envelope parsing that builds the `Google Chat API 500: ...` message.
- Full-repo `tsgo` lanes left to CI.

### Impact-surface review

| File | Change | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | chunk loop restructured; send failures now propagate | covered by mock-level + integration regression tests |
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts` | +2 rejection tests; existing fallback test unchanged and green | 6/6 pass |
| `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts` | new integration suite: real HTTP stub, before/after dispatcher-visible outcomes | 3/3 pass; 2 fail on pre-fix source |

### Lint / typecheck / format

```
$ oxlint extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery.test.ts extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.reply-delivery-failure.test.ts   # exit 0
$ tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json (fresh buildinfo)                                                                                                    # 0 errors
$ oxfmt --check <all touched files>                                                                                                                                         # correct format
$ git diff --check origin/main                                                                                                                                              # clean
```

Base: 76e97ddcdb515f2af781a4b146d9e47eaacdf9e2 (`origin/main`). Head: a1cb28d8b3253761dd48e36bc51f426cd204787c.

target.title: fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When downloading a Google-generated video fails with an HTTP error status, the response body stream remains unread, causing a resource leak.

**Root Cause**: The `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` function in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts` throws on `!response.ok` without cancelling the response body stream. The unread stream lingers until GC.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw, matching the pattern used in google-oauth provider.

**What changed**: One line added before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` to cancel the response body stream.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to retry logic, error handling flow, response parsing, or any other part of the download pipeline. The fix is minimal and scoped strictly to stream cleanup on the error path.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When downloading a generated video from Google's API returns an HTTP error (non-2xx, such as 400 Bad Request or 500 Internal Server Error), the response body stream is left unread, causing a resource/memory leak. The response body may contain error details but is never consumed, resulting in the Node.js HTTP client holding onto the socket until garbage collection. This can lead to resource exhaustion under repeated error conditions.

**Root Cause**: The `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` function in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts` (line 247) throws an error on `!response.ok` without cancelling the response body stream. The unread stream remains open until garbage collection, wasting memory and potentially keeping connections alive unnecessarily. Other providers (e.g., google-oauth) already follow the pattern of cancelling the body before throwing.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the download error, ensuring the stream is properly closed. The optional chaining (`?.`) handles null body; the `.catch(() => undefined)` guards against cancellation rejection masking the original error. This matches the established pattern used in google-oauth provider for consistency across the codebase.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js (via tsx), OpenClaw worktree

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx scripts/evidence-video.ts`

**After-fix evidence**: `docs/.local/pr-109978/verify.log` — all 5 tests pass (body cancel errors on 400/401/403/429/500, cancel before throw, error preserved)

**Observed result after the fix**: Body cancelled before throw on all error status codes (400, 401, 403, 429, 500); cancel rejection does not mask original download error; null body edge case handled by optional chaining.

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end Google API integration (requires API keys and network access). The simulation validates the exact one-line code contract change in isolation.

## Tests and validation

```
--- Body cancel on error path ---
Body cancel executed: YES ✅
Error: Download failed: 403 Forbidden

--- Original error preserved ---
Error: Video generation failed (500)

--- All HTTP error status codes ---
Status 400: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 401: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 403: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 429: body cancelled=OK ✅
Status 500: body cancelled=OK ✅

COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

Closes #107861

Disclosure: AI was used to understand the codebase and review the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack users with a custom outbound username or icon would lose portable draft-preview streaming when native streaming transport was disabled. Long-running top-level DM requests showed lifecycle reactions but no live preview, even though final replies still arrived.

target.title: feat: ask_user — structured questions from the agent with web card, channel buttons, and text answers
target.body:
Related: #109724 (Codex-parity slice 1: this PR is the provider-neutral question RPC that PR deliberately deferred)

## What Problem This Solves

Agents had no first-class way to ask the human a structured question and wait for the answer. The embedded agent could only guess or write prose questions into chat; Codex harness questions got a text-only prompt on channels; and there was no provider-neutral pause/prompt/resume primitive that web UI and message channels could share (the pattern Claude Code ships as `AskUserQuestion` and Codex ships as `request_user_input`).

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the provider-neutral question runtime deferred by #109724, modeled on the existing exec-approval subsystem (the established blocking pause→prompt→resume template):

- **Gateway question runtime**: transient in-memory `question.request` / `question.waitAnswer` / `question.resolve` / `question.get` / `question.list` RPCs plus `question.requested` / `question.resolved` broadcasts under a new `operator.questions` scope (additive; no protocol version bump). Answers are validated against the stored record (unknown ids, cardinality, option membership) and canonicalized before terminalizing; `isSecret` and duplicate option labels are rejected at the request boundary.
- **`ask_user` tool** for the embedded agent (main sessions only, not subagents): 1–3 questions, 2–4 options each (labels ≤64 chars), `multiSelect`, free-text "Other" always available, recommended-option-first convention, `timeoutSeconds` 30–3600 (default 900). The tool blocks like exec approvals; expiry returns a `no_answer` result telling the model to proceed with best judgment.
- **Chat delivery**: the question is delivered to the originating conversation while the tool blocks — as a `MessagePresentation` with native tap-to-answer buttons via a new runtime-authored `{type:"question"}` presentation action (Telegram inline keyboards `tgq1:` ≤64 bytes, Discord custom ids `ocq` ≤100 chars, Slack Block Kit `slq1:`), degrading to numbered text on button-less channels. A plain text reply (number, label, or free text) answers on any channel; the reply is consumed as the answer instead of steering into the run.
- **Control UI**: one unified in-thread question card serving both gateway `ask_user` questions (broadcast-driven, click/multi-select/free-text, resolve over the gateway, terminal states incl. answered-elsewhere/expired) and the existing Codex stream questions from #109724 (composer submit path unchanged).

Codex upstream contract checked directly at `openai/codex@9ff47868eb`: `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/request_user_input.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1585-1637` (schema conventions: header ≤12 chars, recommended-first, forced free-text "Other", root-thread-only — mirrored here). Converging the Codex/Copilot harness bridges onto this runtime is a named follow-up, not part of this PR.

## User Impact

Agents can now pause and ask a real question with buttons. Users answer by clicking in the web Control UI, tapping a native button on Telegram/Discord/Slack, or just replying in text on any channel; the agent resumes with structured answers. Docs: `docs/tools/ask-user.md`.

Pending card (web):
![pending](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/01-question-pending.png)
Answered:
![answered](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/02-question-answered.png)
MultiSelect:
![multiselect](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/03-question-multiselect.png)
Terminal states (answered elsewhere / expired):
![terminal](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/04-question-terminal-states.png)

## Evidence

- **Live end-to-end proof** on a source-checkout gateway (isolated `--dev` state dir, `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`): agent called `ask_user` with a single-select + multiSelect pair, blocked 1m03s, the web card rendered in-thread, options were clicked (Staging + Integration/E2E), the gateway resolved, and the agent resumed enumerating exactly those answers. This live run also caught and fixed a gating bug (`isEmbeddedMode()` is the TUI-host flag, not the embedded-runner flag — `ask_user` was invisible to normal gateway runs until commit `ce0251e6bb9`'s fix).
- **Playwright e2e** `ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts` (3 tests, mock gateway): render → resolve payload shape (`{answers:{deploy_target:{answers:["Staging (Recommended)"]}}}`) → resolved state; multiSelect arrays; answered-elsewhere + expired terminal states. Screenshots above are its artifacts.
- **Focused suites** (local, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`): gateway question manager + RPC handlers + protocol validators, ask_user tool (normalize/execute/claim/abort races), subscriber delivery, outbound presentation precedence, per-channel envelope round-trips incl. byte limits, UI prompt state machine + card + thread placement — all green (500+ tests across the touched files).
- **Typecheck/lint**: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, targeted oxlint — green (Testbox + local fallback when Testbox returned 429).
- **Build**: full `pnpm build` green, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`.
- **Autoreview** (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): three iterations; 7 findings accepted and fixed (answer validation at resolve, isSecret fail-closed, duplicate-label rejection, UI retry latch, reconnect `QUESTION_NOT_FOUND` terminalization, option-label bound, answer canonicalization); final run clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

Follow-ups (intentionally out of scope): converge Codex/Copilot harness user-input bridges onto the question runtime; reaction-based answering on WhatsApp/Signal/iMessage; unbind channel buttons after resolution; MCP elicitation routing (pending the 2026-07-28 MRTR spec).

target.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks
target.body:
Closes #109435

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agent runs repeatedly issuing the same blocked tool call could never reach the configured global circuit breaker after critical loop blocking began. Critical tool-loop vetoes were excluded from no-progress accounting, freezing the streak below the higher global threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool-loop vetoes are recorded as an explicit no-progress outcome and counted toward the current unchanged-result streak. A later changed result resets earlier vetoes so recovered runs are not stopped prematurely. Policy, approval, abort, and other blocked outcomes remain distinct, and run-termination policy remains out of scope.

## User Impact

Repeated blocked tool calls now continue through the configured escalation path, allowing the global circuit breaker to trigger at its threshold. If a tool later makes progress, vetoes from the older stalled segment no longer count against the recovered run.

## Evidence

The production `detectToolCallLoop`, `recordToolCall`, and `recordToolCallOutcome` path was exercised against a real `SessionState` with 20 identical no-progress results followed by ten tool-loop vetoes.

Before the patch, the regression remains at `generic_repeat` because vetoes do not advance the streak. After the patch, the same sequence advances from 20 through 30 and reaches the global breaker on the tenth veto:

```console
[agents/loop-detection] Critical generic loop detected: read repeated 20 times
after-real-outcomes=generic_repeat:20
[agents/loop-detection] Critical generic loop detected: read repeated 21 times
after-veto-1=generic_repeat:21
[agents/loop-detection] Critical generic loop detected: read repeated 29 times
after-veto-9=generic_repeat:29
after-veto-10=global_circuit_breaker:30
[agents/loop-detection] Global circuit breaker triggered: read repeated 30 times with no progress
```

Validation completed:

```console
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts
# 58 detector tests and 84 end-to-end tests passed

pnpm check:test-types
# passed all core, extension, and root test typechecks

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
# passed
```

The changed-result regression additionally verifies that progress resets older vetoes, so a recovered run does not inherit the stalled segment's count. The changed-file gate reached a repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline failure that reproduces on clean `origin/main`; this PR does not touch that surface.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: tool-loop vetoes froze the no-progress streak after critical blocking, making the global circuit breaker unreachable.
- Real environment tested: macOS with Node 24.16, exercising the production loop-detection module against a real `SessionState`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: a `node --import tsx --input-type=module` probe imported `detectToolCallLoop`, `recordToolCall`, and `recordToolCallOutcome`, recorded 20 identical results, then recorded ten `loop-veto` outcomes while printing each detector verdict.
- Evidence after fix: the copied terminal output above shows streak 20 after real outcomes, 21 after the first veto, 29 after the ninth veto, and `global_circuit_breaker:30` after the tenth veto.
- Observed result after fix: the global breaker becomes reachable while critical blocking remains sticky before the final threshold.
- What was not tested: a full provider-backed agent turn running until the breaker; the production-function probe covers the exact detector and session-state path repaired here.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: actual run termination remains intentionally out of scope for this PR.

target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

The established codebase pattern is to cancel the response body before throwing on non-ok responses (see `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, etc.). This fix applies the same pattern to the Telegram Mini App page handler.

The change is purely mechanical — `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` — following existing codebase convention. The body stream is unread after a non-ok response, so cancelling it is the correct cleanup action with no behavioral side effects.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Resources are cleaned up immediately on auth error instead of dangling until garbage collection.

## Test Results

All 18 tests across 7 test files pass, including the two page-specific tests and the auth-timeout simulation:

```
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.auth-timeout.test.ts (1 test)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.test.ts (6 tests)

```

## Runtime Evidence Note

This fix is a mechanical change that applies the existing `body?.cancel()` pattern in a single location. Real Telegram Mini App runtime evidence (e.g., confirming the body is cancelled in a live Telegram WebView environment) requires a live Telegram bot setup with Mini App configured, which is not available in the automation pipeline. The change is verified at the code level by:

- Conformance to the established codebase pattern (same idiom used across multiple extensions)
- Unit test coverage (page rendering + auth timeout edge case)
- Static analysis: the `cancel()` call is a no-op when the body is already consumed or null, and `.catch(() => undefined)` prevents unhandled rejections — both standard defensive patterns in this codebase
